layout._comment_drawer: An open drawer re-lays the world: the surface rises (not above skyMin) so that at least sectionMin rows of section stay above the drawer; the section is cropped there (top layers at full scale + a history ribbon), rulerW world px at the right are the era ruler.

niche._comment: Life arises on its own (core/niche.ts). The surface of each zone is read every geology tick: the shares of material groups in its top surfaceRows rows. A species' suitability is the product over its needs of min(1, have / need) (food: 1 if any of its foods lives, else 0); its niche opens when every need is met at least openAt, and once lived in it holds while every need is met at least closeAt. Then up to round(wild × suitability) units (at least 1) arise on their own — or, for a species with wildShare, round(wildShare × the capacity of its zones × suitability): a forest fills the land its soil allows — one every growSec seconds (faster for a big niche: growSec / max(1, cap / 8)) where there is room; when the niche shrinks, one wild unit dies every declineSec. Drought multiplies the suitability of shore and land life by drought, a glacier all life by glacier.

press._comment: Press (brief 5, A2): hold a layer >holdMs to squeeze it: compaction x6, transformations x4 in a circle of `radius` world px (+ Wide Press). Costs costShare of the income per second.

burial._comment: Burial window (brief 5, В2): >= killed violent deaths within windowYears game years opens it for `seconds` real seconds; a flood or a volcano cast in it makes bones from before..after years around now fossilise fossilMul times as easily.

sand._comment: The falling-sand strata (core/sand.ts, pressure.ts, beds.ts, world/Grid.ts, Archive.ts). One particle = 2x2 world pixels. Rows count from the top of the grid. bedRows: bedrock rows at the bottom (under the bottom menu); the thing lies on the bedrock, artifactW x artifactH particles; sinkRow = the row right above the thing: the oldest rock there sinks into the archive as a whole row when the mean column above it is taller than sinkLine x refRows (raw count, the press does not change the level); the rate is sinkRate x overload^4 rows per second, full when sinkRockShare of the row is rock, a quarter when none is. pressurePerParticle: MPa of each particle above per unit of density (calibrated in merge stage 2). gradientPerRow: degrees per particle row of depth. oxygenRows: organic matter rots this close to the surface. waterFallEvery: in water a particle falls every Nth step; waterSlipMul scales its slide chance. cellsPerParticle: how many old 1x1 cells one particle stands for in the archive (2x2). archiveMaxRows: an archive layer closes after this many rows (mean); archiveMaxLayers: above this the oldest layers of one epoch merge into a belt. pile: the pile a tap drops (base + perLevel particles). coatDepth: how deep a marker bed reaches down a steep face. coatWait: seconds a bed waits for falling particles to land. seaAboveLine: the water line stands this many rows higher than the level where the mean of the relief (see relief) lies on the line where the strata settle. bedCooldown: seconds between two ochre beds of the «Bed» button. archiveDigShare: the share of the archive's (compacted) thickness the tribe digs through in epoch VII. rockYieldMul: rock paid for a transformation of a visible particle (× yield × rockYield × cellsPerParticle); below 1 because the visible strata turn to rock sooner than the old cells did. archiveYieldMul: the same for the transformations of the archive of the depth; below 1 because the piles of taps add matter the old game did not have (calibrated in merge stage 5). startBelowLine: a migrated old save starts with the strata filled up to this many rows below the line; a new world starts on the old ground this many rows below its relief. relief: the shape the drizzle of sediment keeps, in rows below the water line (sea floor, shore, land; negative = above the water), blended across zone borders; sediment falls where there is room under that shape, and where a column is full it is carried to the nearest column with room with the most room, less one row for every spill columns of distance (a delta that reaches the hollows of the land), so the sea stays a sea and the land stays dry whatever the life lays down. stepsPerSecond: physics steps a second on screen (falling and sliding speed); stepsPerSecondLow: the same with quality «low» (weak phones). creep: the chance a still grain slides down a free 45° slope each physics step (peaks settle to the natural angle); peakCrumble: the same for a lone grain on a peak with nothing at its sides. slump: the chance a still grain slides two cells aside and one down (≈27°) each step: a fresh cone slumps into a mound. pileSkyRow / pileDrop: a tapped pile appears pileDrop rows above the ground of its column, never higher than row pileSkyRow (under the header).

fluids._comment: Oil and gas creep up through porous beds and stop under seals (core/fluids.ts). tickHz: migration ticks a second; oilChance / gasChance: the chance a particle tries to move in a tick; slopeChance: the chance it finds a way up past the edge of a seal in a tick; sideChance: the chance it slides along under a seal when it cannot rise; tight: materials a fluid passes only now and then (× tightMul); seals: materials nothing passes through.

lenses._comment: Buried water and geysers (core/fluids.ts). Every about every seconds (randomised ±50 %) a stretch of shallow water (1..shallowRows deep, wMin..wMax columns) leaves a lens of water particles on its floor (1 row at the edges, 2 in the middle) for the next laminae to bury; at most maxParticles water particles in the strata. A lens of at least minLens particles with a particle at least eruptDepth rows under the surface breaks out with the chance eruptChance a second (+ per extra row eruptPerRow): its whole lens goes up through the vent above its top as a geyser, the empty lens collapses, and sinterPer particles of sinter (one per sinterPer water particles, at most sinterMax) fall around the vent. Not in the headless run (no effect on the balance).

absorb._comment: The thing absorbs the strata: the bottom squeezeRows rows of the visible strata and then the bandRows rows the conveyor took are drawn squeezed into the height of squeezeRows rows, each line thinner than the one above it by the same ratio (2 px at the top, a fraction of a pixel at the bottom: the lower, the denser); the lowest line touches the thing and is absorbed. Energy of a line = sum over its particles of value × (flat × energyMul + incomePerSec × incomeShare). value: by kind (loose, rock, marker), then by material (overrides); a fossil bone × fossilMul.
